title: Preserve pending ApplyPatch approval across checkpoints
body:
A direct, approval-required ApplyPatch call can be waiting for the application when Python saves a portable checkpoint. Core previously treated cancellation of that waiter as a fatal tool failure, so the checkpoint could not be written.

Python now passes the exact pending ApplyPatch IDs for the current turn to the existing portable suspension. Core omits a result only when the patch is still waiting for approval and its dispatch has stopped and joined. A completed sibling keeps its original Shell or ApplyPatch output. Restoring a pending patch still requires a new decision.

The change also defers managed Shell and ApplyPatch lifecycle callbacks until approval. The tests check that rejection causes no effect, approval runs the callbacks in order, and restore rejects changes to the saved action or its owner.

The pinned native build passed 86 focused tests. The combined tests on the current branch passed 255 tests with one skip. Four Rust tests passed, including the check that a shutdown timeout cannot authorize a checkpoint.

The exact [hosted Linux x64 build](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/43634917338/job/132569584335) passed 71 focused tests locally after I verified the wheel and source hashes. These covered managed tool approval, pending ApplyPatch and Shell restore, and custom storage.

The full local wrapper passed format, lint, and type checks. Its parallel test phase reported 12,367 passes, 394 skips, and 18 failures outside the changed files. Seven reproduce fixture failures addressed in #6009. The storage example passed after pinning its subprocess to this checkout. The telemetry case also passed in isolation. All four [CodeQL jobs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/43634917039) passed in 13m57s including queue time.

The [hosted Tests workflow](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/43634917338) passed all four native builds and all four installed-package checks. The SDK suites reported 28 distinct failures across Linux, macOS, and Windows. The companion fixture PR #6009 fixes 27 of those cases, verified against the canonical native wheel. title: Avoid repeated work in provider-managed history
body:
### Summary

This pull request speeds up provider-managed history for large, multi-round conversations. Core has been re-serializing and hashing unchanged user text even after the provider has acknowledged it. A bounded cache on each history cursor reuses the exact JSON byte count and digest when the text matches. The digest lookup also checks the item ID and phase. Core still applies its existing item and byte limits.

Core has also been building a thread snapshot on metadata writes whose callers discard it. The in-memory store now applies those writes under the existing lock and skips the snapshot. Public metadata updates still return their owned snapshot. The SDK still records memory-mode changes after a successful write.

The change modifies two existing Codex patches and adds none.

### Test plan

The release-PGO comparison used independent fresh conversations and a loopback Responses server. Each conversation sent 512 KiB of input, made five real Python tool calls, and returned a 16 KiB response. Each v1 arm used buffered HTTP. The table shows p50 latency and all-client CPU in milliseconds across 960 measured conversations.

| Build | Latency | CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| v0.24.0 | 120.20 | 70.13 |
| Current v1, full replay | 100.38 | 63.52 |
| Current v1, provider-managed history | 133.89 | 104.77 |
| Candidate, provider-managed history | 86.44 | 55.18 |

The paired reductions were 35.5% in latency and 47.6% in CPU versus current provider-managed history. The candidate kept the same request bodies and sent about 83% fewer request bytes than full replay. The 480-conversation escaped-text control also passed. Its linked latency fell from 171.85 to 112.08 ms and CPU from 131.45 to 70.11 ms.

All six default-streaming guardrails passed across 7,200 fresh conversations with provider-managed history disabled. The guardrails used a predeclared 5% limit on paired point estimates for p50, p95, and CPU. The candidate still trailed v0 on this workload.

- The installed candidate passed 92 provider-history, storage, and checkpoint tests.
- Three isolated Rust tests verified exact byte counts, digest matches, and fallback. The publication source adds those cases under `#[cfg(test)]`. The prepared production source matches the benchmark build.
- Hosted checks and the full local verification are pending.

title: Native HTTP/2 streaming with buffered HTTP/1.1
body:
### Summary

Native streaming has been using HTTP/1.1 because the TLS client has not been advertising HTTP/2 through ALPN. The change has been enabling HTTP/2 negotiation for streaming and keeping buffered responses on HTTP/1.1. Each provider has been applying the same policy to pooled, unpooled, and fallback clients. Buffered requests have been keeping HTTP/1.1 after checkpoint restore as well.

One existing Codex patch modified, with zero new patch files.

### Benchmark

| SDK | Median latency | Client CPU per conversation |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| v0.24.0 | 11.04 ms | 9.99 ms |
| v1 baseline (`21367c8`) | 18.47 ms | 19.16 ms |
| v1 with this transport policy (`17999ff`) | 13.41 ms | 14.14 ms |

The streaming workload has been showing 27.4% lower median latency and 26.2% lower CPU versus the pinned v1 baseline. The buffered control has been staying within 0.3% of baseline on both measures. All six prespecified gates have been passing in both comparisons.

The streaming comparison has been covering 1,200 independent fresh conversations per SDK in 12 balanced blocks, with one real tool call and a 16 KiB response. Each worker has been reusing its provider. The v0 final-result adapter has been using JSON, and v1 has been using SSE. Client CPU has been including Python and Rust threads and excluding the peer process.

### Test plan

- Two Core fallback tests, one Rust provider isolation test, and ten installed SDK tests passing on the benchmark revision.
- Functional checks passing for HTTP/2 streaming, HTTP/1.1 fallback, buffered HTTP/1.1, and concurrent conversation isolation.
- Independent source review of the branch integration and Windows ClientHello test fix.
- Forced pool rejection check passing with three independent conversations on the benchmark revision.
- On the pre-fix merge commit (`108657ac`), format, lint, type checks, and 11,977 local sandbox tests passing. All 29 ordinary CI checks passing.
- The new TLS regression has been reproducing the checkpoint bug against that pre-fix wheel. title: Close native Python SDK parity
body:
### Summary

After a native Agent handoff, the provider request has been retaining the source Agent's output strictness even when the destination declares a different setting. The runtime has been reading strictness from the active Agent declaration. An explicit per-turn override still takes precedence, and reopening a saved session keeps its recorded model identity.

Hosted WebSocket turns have also been dropping queued tool calls when a completed frame arrived before a later rejection. The transport has been admitting calls from the completed response in order, while keeping deduplication and cancellation with the existing turn owner.

This draft has been tracking the remaining native Python parity work. It covers provider compatibility, handoffs and tools, persistence, sandbox execution, tracing, and platform verification.

The native runtime now records the configured child declaration on each live call and result and on results produced after recovery. Hosted WebSocket history retains usage per physical request.

Preapproved HTTP MCP now works through CustomStorage and keeps the result across cold reopen without repeating the tool. Native retry callbacks now expose the admitted provider replay classification directly.

The native SDK now preserves signed LiteLLM thinking through buffered and streamed requests and a cold checkpoint. The restored native history also supports historical shell output identity. An application can observe native events during a one-shot run and recover invalid terminal output after its observer has finished. The signed reasoning and recovery suite passed 41 tests. A subsequent recovery and cancellation suite passed 25 tests.

Ordinary managed MCP servers can opt into best-effort strict tool schemas. The runtime keeps the original non-strict path when it cannot convert a schema without losing constraints or exceeding the configured size. The exact build has been passing 128 native MCP, recovery, reasoning, and legacy shell tests.

The native LiteLLM adapter now accepts its supported enabled thinking options. Gemini tool calls preserve their private thought signatures through buffered and streamed continuation, including cold restore. The adapter rejects signatures from other provider families before any local tool runs. The exact SDK tree passed 23 native provider tests and five host admission tests.

The benchmark has been comparing normal PGO builds of v1 baseline `9ff2112` and candidate `687a270`, using independent fresh conversations against a local model peer. The original reply expires. If a live code cell prevents checkpointing, the Session keeps the original turn and reply available.

Native sandbox events carry port numbers, process exit codes, and liveness results with each subscriber's output limit. An existing borrowed workspace can open with its current manifest. Changes to its entries require an atomic provider transaction. The SDK rejects unsupported changes before materialization and validates the gateway's working directory on Windows and POSIX.

MCP declarations preserve their default failure handling when copied as data. An explicit `None` still raises the original failure, and an application callback stays bound to the selected server. `Agent` keeps its existing positional field order.

`DockerGateway` has been replacing the handwritten connection callback for fresh SDK-owned Linux containers. It has been using the selected client's explicit Unix socket, the exact container ID, and Core's existing stdio connection owner. The helper has been connecting to a compatible exec-server already installed in that image. Borrowed, resumed and snapshot-created containers, custom daemon authentication, and remote Docker transports have been continuing through application gateways.

Composed capability and Agent context callbacks have been sharing the live native admission predicate, with checks between components after awaited work. title: fix(codex): Recover dead child turns without replaying work
body:
### Summary

An application can reopen the original local session after a child or grandchild dies. When the saved history accounts for the affected turns, the SDK records the interruption. It keeps the original IDs and leaves the children stopped. Writer locks protect against a second process reopening the same work during recovery.

Before sending a model request, the SDK records whether it can start provider-hosted work. Automatic recovery requires a receipt that rules out such work for the original thread and turn. An older or missing receipt leaves the turn on hold. Callers can still submit a reconciliation receipt for an exact retained invocation. The SDK also checks for unfinished hosted tools and native commands before it records an interruption.

title: Skipping empty, uncaptured WebSocket probability facts
body:
Empty, uncaptured probability facts from WebSocket responses have been taking a queue-and-acknowledgement round trip before disposal. This patch has been skipping that wait after response interception, while preserving requested probability capture, malformed or nonempty facts, and cooperative scheduling.

The fixed comparison has been failing the predeclared retention gate. WebSocket CPU has been improving by 16.8%, with 4.4% lower median latency. However, the p95 latency ratio's 95% upper bound has been reaching 1.0706, above the 1.05 limit. The buffered control has been exceeding the same bound for p95 latency (1.0573), whole-run wall time (1.0559), and whole-run CPU (1.0554). All point-estimate checks have been passing; these intervals have been leaving regression risk unresolved rather than demonstrating those regressions.

Per fresh conversation, in milliseconds: median latency / client CPU.

| Cohort | v0 | Current v1 | Candidate v1 |

| WebSocket | 10.44 / 9.85 | 21.65 / 33.14 | 20.68 / 27.57 |

Each cohort has been comparing three arms across 12 matched process blocks. Each arm and block has been contributing 100 measured fresh conversations and one prefill. title: Stage input when restoring a native manual checkpoint
body:
### Summary

A paused native run can accept new input while an application is completing a manual tool action. `SessionState.with_pending_input()` stages that input in order and keeps repeated items. `without_pending_input()` clears the batch before a retry.

After the manual reply is accepted, the SDK waits for the destination input guardrails. Core writes the staged input after the reply and clears the batch after the history write finishes. If a guardrail rejects the batch, the application can save a retry checkpoint. It retains the accepted reply and its private application data, and the next open resumes the same turn without issuing the manual request again.

This change covers native checkpoints with local history.

title: fix: Preserve trace ownership for deferred child follow-ups
body:
### Summary

Deferred follow-ups can start a child turn after the previous turn finishes. The child now keeps the caller's trace parent and capture policy when every message in the admitted batch has one verified owner. Mixed or unknown owners get a fresh scope with tracing and sensitive capture disabled. Queue-only messages contribute to the decision without keeping an ended sender's trace storage alive.

Core seals the batch before the turn-start hook. Messages accepted while registration is pending stay queued in order for a later wake. Queue-only messages leave the child idle until a wake is otherwise eligible. Messages accepted by an already registered turn keep the existing delivery behavior.

A committed close can revoke a held mailbox start when the submission queue is full. The loop still processes previously accepted direct submissions before closing. Revoked starts cannot publish a Python admission receipt or consume their mailbox prefix. An interrupt or mailbox submission rejected during teardown leaves the old runtime registered until its session loop exits.

title: Wait for the reloaded child turn before taking its snapshot
body:
The Windows Python 3.14 job exposed a race in the cold-child recovery fixture. The manual grant can arrive before the reloaded child’s `Turn` is observable, so a snapshot taken at grant delivery can capture an active child without its turn. [Failing Windows job](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/42974637568/job/130385397113)

The fixture now takes the snapshot after `request.respond()` has observed the turn and compares the snapshot’s submission and turn IDs with the request. It still checks that the stale incarnation cannot answer the grant and that the live reply validates once and completes.

- Independent implementation review found no blockers. The signed commit contains the single reviewed test file.

title: Fix ordering across overlapping Python trace losses

title: Fix SDK platform tests and Linux workspace discovery
body:
### Summary

This pull request fixes failures in the ordinary SDK tests on Windows, Python 3.10, and macOS. It also fixes a Linux sandbox setup race that can hide the nearest Git root from workspace guidance discovery.

Importing Modal selects a Windows event loop that cannot start subprocesses. The native test fixtures use a pytest-asyncio `ProactorEventLoop` factory on Windows so they can start OpenSSL and the exec server. [Python Windows subprocess support](https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/asyncio-platforms.html#subprocess-support-on-windows) · [Billing-free Windows job](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/42784551206/job/129748851386)

The session resume, failed-flush recovery, and early-opening privacy tests use a process-local custom store. The raw-history reopen test retains SQLite on POSIX and uses the same process-local store on Windows. The SQLite adapter requires POSIX file locking.

Python 3.10 can drop the original cancellation message when a caller awaits a cancelled task. The tests capture the exception inside the task to check its message and context. They also check that cancellation reaches the caller and cleanup still happens. [Python cancellation message behavior](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.Task.cancel)

The executor transform tests leave room for Windows clock granularity while preserving their expiry and cleanup checks. The plan usage test allows one reported Python clock tick at the upper wall-clock bound.

On Windows, the real MongoDB tests run after the parallel workers exit. The fixture keeps its 20-second startup bound and reports early exits or live startup timeouts with process logs. After readiness, the test client has a separate five-second operation bound.

The tracing fixtures bind numeric loopback without a reverse lookup and warm the transport before measuring deadlines and batching. The exporter tests retain the 30-second subprocess watchdog, 200 ms native deadline, 750 ms batch budget, and 500 ms measured response delay. They check batch delivery, peer closure, cleanup, and cancellation diagnostics.

The native CLI resolves the two `TypedDict` input annotations before restoring their Classic module identity. This gives Pydantic the concrete `Literal` tags on Python 3.14. The generated API fixture records the equivalent declarations.

The Windows opening test checks the platform rejection and retains its cleanup assertions. The sandboxed image-read fixture runs on Linux and macOS, where the real executor supports it. The positive environment fixture sends valid distinct names on Windows. The ordinary real-child control includes captured output if the child exits unsuccessfully. On Windows, that fixture supplies the host's `SYSTEMROOT` explicitly so Python 3.10 can initialize with environment inheritance disabled.

The Linux overlay preserves protected metadata during sandbox mount setup. Workspace guidance can still find the nearest project root for a Git directory or linked worktree, and real protected metadata stays read-only.

### Test plan

- The earlier Windows and Python 3.10 fixes reduced the ordinary Windows failures to the remaining timing, MongoDB, and tracing cases. [Windows 3.10](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/42811158407/job/129831995314) · [Windows 3.14](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/42811158407/job/129831995359)

The server can consume a saved-login refresh token before it returns a replacement. If all waiting turns cancel and provider shutdown stops the exchange, the cache keeps the spent token and a new process cannot open a Session.

body:
Bumps [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) from 9.0.3 to 9.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Updates the requirements on [python-multipart](https://github.com/Kludex/python-multipart) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from python-multipart's releases.

Version 0.0.33

🛡️ Safer form parsing

This release lets you cap URL-encoded form fields as they stream in, and fixes several upload and decoding edge cases. It also drops Python 3.10 and adds Python 3.15.

pip install python-multipart==0.0.33
  • Limit URL-encoded fields while streaming (#333). The new opt-in MAX_FIELDS and MAX_FIELD_SIZE options for FormParser raise FormParserError before oversized data is buffered. Both default to no limit, and multipart forms are unaffected.
  • Nameless uploads no longer crash when spilled to disk (#343). Uploads without a filename used to raise AttributeError when UPLOAD_KEEP_EXTENSIONS or UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME was set.
  • UPLOAD_DIR accepts str with UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME (#335). A str upload directory used to fail on the first write to disk.
  • Decoded data is complete before callbacks run (#336, #355). Content-Transfer-Encoding decoders are finalized at the end of each part, and quoted-printable escapes split across writes decode correctly.
  • parse_options_header lowercases content types with parameters (#287). Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=abc now returns multipart/form-data, the same as headers without parameters.

⚡ Faster parsing

  • Faster opening boundary matching (#328). Complete boundaries are matched in one step.
  • Faster parser state lookups (#330). Parser states are module-level enum members, so their repr is now multipart.END instead of <MultipartState.END: 12>.
  • Faster querystring callback dispatch (#316).

🐍 Python support

  • Python 3.10 is no longer supported (#329). Python 3.11 is now the minimum.
  • Python 3.15 is supported (#350).

💜 Thank you

Thanks to @​Edneam, @​sungbin1015, @​carlok, and @​fjvbn2003 for contributing to this release.

Thanks to the individual sponsors who contributed $134.00 to support this work. If python-multipart is useful to you, consider sponsoring me on GitHub.

title: Add Sign in with ChatGPT plan auth for native agents
body:
### Summary

`NativeProvider` supports ChatGPT plan billing through `SignInWithChatGPT` for eligible registered integrations. After authenticating the user and authorizing conversation access, the application returns one immutable `SignInWithChatGPTCredentials` snapshot from the protected OAuth record. The snapshot carries the verified issuer, issued client ID, account subject, and current bearer. [Sign in with ChatGPT inference](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference)

The SDK checks the verified account binding before returning saved history or pending calls. The same account can resume after a bearer-only refresh. Structured-output repair keeps the original session credentials. The SDK separately checks the bearer's resource, scope, expiry, and registration and sends it to the fixed streaming Responses endpoint. The application receives authentication and quota failures and controls retries. API-key billing requires explicit selection.

Registered streams admit provisional tool calls into history and execution after successful completion. For HTTP admission and capability failures, `NativeError` retains the observed status and request ID. A documented unsupported-capability response also exposes its bounded request field path as `NativeError.param`. The example shows how to supply the protected record. The native build retains durable saved Codex login refresh and shutdown from [#5720](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/5720) and nearest Git-root discovery from [#5721](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/5721).

### Test plan

- On signed head `8b3d08d4`, the regenerated alpha.7 API snapshot matched the combined source and preserved the registered billing and strict local read-root signatures. All 12 focused source tests and seven-file Ruff lint and format checks passed. Independent replay matched all 123 Core overlays and three RMCP overlays. The landed WebSocket and saved-login quota patches remain intact.
- A matching Linux x64 wheel for the earlier SDK tree `a237d68e` passed 63 installed tests with zero skips. Synthetic coverage included explicit registered routing, credential isolation, same-account restore after bearer renewal, typed quota and throttle attention before stream EOF, exact request counts, transient API-key recovery, and sealed checkpoints.
- Earlier synthetic HTTP 403 and 400 probes sent one request each and retained recovery diagnostics while keeping the bearer out of public errors.
- [Current hosted Tests](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/42913345476) are pending. Current installed verification requires a matching native artifact. Live bearer acceptance and quota debit require an authorized registered test account.
